principles.text: Start with a high-touch service business to learn the market and get cash flow, then productize what works across clients.
Price your first product low as a trust tripwire, then raise prices as you deliver results.
Presell before building: only build once enough people have paid for it.
Pick one platform you enjoy, master it, then add the next; say one thing a thousand ways.
Design your life first and build a business that supports it; optimize for profit and time, not scale.

sampleQA.question: How should I price my first digital product?

answer.text: Charge $50 to $150 at first: affordable enough to get buyers without years of trust-building.
Treat it as a trust tripwire, then sell higher-priced offers to those customers.
Give each course one price, not tiers or bundles, to avoid decision fatigue.
Keep it short: teach what people want in 45 minutes or less to raise completion.

sampleQA.question: When should I quit my job to go solo?

answer.text: Get side income to roughly 60-70% of your take-home pay before quitting.
Save runway, build pipeline first, leave without burning bridges, and have a risk plan.
Keep your job and start on the side rather than blowing up a steady paycheck overnight.

sampleQA.question: How do I grow on LinkedIn from zero?

answer.text: Pick a tight sub-niche and talk about it every day so people know who you serve.
Comment thoughtfully on 9 relevant posts daily, and get there first with value under bigger creators.
Use a Teach, Teach, Teach, Sell mix: 80% value, 20% soft promotion.
Spend the 210 characters above 'see more' breaking the scroll; the first line matters most.
